digest.component_or_area: test infrastructure - ACLI subprocess timeout and snapshot fetch stall sentinels
propositions: Blanket autouse _short_timeout fixture with 1s timeout/1s grace/1s drain causes five real-subprocess reap tests to burn ~1.01s each waiting for deadline expiry, creating flaky timing dependencies on interpreter startup speed.

test_run_acli_429_retries_with_rate_limit_backoff inherits the 1s ceiling as implicit pass condition, creating a latent load flake where slower runners fail if two sequential spawns cannot complete within the shared module-wide window.
Reap tests assert on child-side setup (pidfile, spawn counter, flushed stdout) whose ordering against timeout relies on wall-clock luck rather than explicit ordering, creating load-dependent races.
tight_stall injects a 2s low-speed window when sibling tests prove git honors a 1s window, wasting test time without added coverage.
Split fixture approach with explicit readiness gates and process-specific timeout ceilings removes timing races by making child setup observable rather than timing-dependent.
